title: Test bt_audio.sh to its reachable ceiling, and fix the timeout bug the tests found
objective: Finish the bluetooth family, the fourth of the sixteen untested fixes/lib libs and the largest at 214 lines. Writing the tests exposed a real production bug -- `timeout 3 _run_as_user wpctl status` can never succeed, because timeout is a binary and _run_as_user is a shell function -- so this lands the fix alongside the coverage rather than testing a broken branch into permanence. The lib reaches 96.97% and stays exempt: the last four lines are pipe operators no test can reach.
acceptance_criteria: bt_audio.sh measures 96.97% (128/132) through lib/tests/run_all.sh, twice, with the same line set both times.
The four uncovered lines are shown to be `} |` pipe operators rather than statements, and shown to execute, before the shortfall is accepted.
shfmt is shown to rewrite HEAD's one-line block form, proving the reformat that raised the denominator is unavoidable rather than something to revert.
The healthy branch of check_pipewire_health is actually reachable: a test asserts 'PipeWire is responsive' and passes, which was impossible before the fix.
meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt is UNCHANGED -- bt_audio.sh does not meet the 100% bar.
Every test file stays under the repo's 250-line cap, and pre-commit passes with no suppression added.
out_of_scope: Clearing bt_audio.sh or bt_adapter.sh from the allowlist. Both are capped by defect (a) in docs/kcov-under-report.md.

Changing continuation_lines() in meta/scripts/lib/shell_coverage_lines.py to exclude `} |` and backslash-continued assignments. It changes the denominator for every measured lib and must land on its own; measured to affect only these two libs.
Reverting shfmt's reformat of bt_audio.sh, which the pre-commit hook would reapply on the next commit touching the file.
The remaining twelve untested fixes/lib libs, none of which carry either continuation-pipe form.
verifier: bash linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/fixes/lib/tests/run_all.sh (expects all files passing, 20 + 15 + 12 for the three bt_audio files), plus bash meta/scripts/shell_coverage_jail.sh --subject linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/fixes/lib/tests/run_all.sh --measure bt_audio.sh --min 1 --fail-on-case-error -- "" (expects 128/132 = 96.97%, uncovered 90 113 137 157), plus bash meta/scripts/check_shell_coverage.sh (expects exit 0, with bt_audio.sh still exempt).
